items.stem: Model risk in an AI/ML system most directly refers to the risk that:

options.text: The model is wrong or misused, leading to adverse outcomes
options.rationale: Correct: model risk is the risk of errors or misuse of the model.
Infrastructure speed is not model risk.
UI preference is not model risk.
Branding is unrelated to model risk.

items.explanation: Correct: model risk is the risk of errors or misuse of the model.

items.stem: Explainability techniques for machine-learning models aim to:

options.text: Make model outputs interpretable to stakeholders
options.rationale: Correct: explainability helps stakeholders understand why a model made a decision.
Encryption is a security control, not explainability.
Validation is still required alongside explainability.

items.explanation: Correct: explainability helps stakeholders understand why a model made a decision.

items.stem: Select TWO good practices in governing AI models used for risk decisions.

options.text: Independent validation of models before and after deployment
options.rationale: Correct: independent validation is a core model-risk control.

options.text: Monitoring for data and concept drift over time
options.rationale: Correct: ongoing monitoring detects performance degradation.

options.text: Allowing anyone to change the production model without review
options.rationale: Uncontrolled changes are a governance failure.
Limitations must be disclosed to decision-makers.

items.explanation: Correct: independent validation is a core model-risk control.
